chapter: Learning the trombone and jam sessions
title: His family and Savannah migrants to New York
summary: He has sisters and half brothers, an uncle Will who played trombone, and says Savannah people went to New York as New Orleans people went to Chicago.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You said your sister studied piano. How many children were there in your family?
Well, I had some half brothers, and then I had three sisters and some half brothers. I have two sisters living now. My half brothers are dead.
And did your sister study -- one sister studied piano?
And you started with trumpet and went to trombone. Was there anybody else in the family who played a --
No, there's this uncle who I didn't really know real well. He was -- played trombone.

Uh-huh. I didn't know him real -- I didn't know him real well. I didn't know too much about him because -- you know, most of the people in Savannah, they left and went to New York. Most of the people in New Orleans, they went to Chicago. I guess there was a direct line from both spots, you know, but most all people from Savannah went to New York. There are more people from -- right today, their roots were in Savannah. They will live in New York.
And just like most people from Louisiana go to Chicago back at that time, it seems. It's probably the way the trains ran or something like that -- a direct line, see.
